gen-irish-grover-gf-cascadia-mono: Irish Grover stands tall and sturdy, its lowercase looking large and its strokes shifting softly in thickness. And Cascadia Mono sits beneath in sans-serif, pin-straight and compact, so the playful heading gets a tidy footing.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-montserrat-alternates: Montserrat Alternates has a wide-open c and round, chalky lowercase. Oxanium above it brings a big x-height and one unbroken line weight, and that shared steadiness is what ties them together.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-lexend-exa: Paprika scatters its letters wide, with lowercase that fills the line almost like capitals, loud and loose. Lexend Exa follows in plain sans, so give it a generous size.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-lexend-mega: Loose, chunky and a bit swaggering. Revalia strides across the line with spaced-out letters, while Lexend Mega underneath draws every stem and arc in lockstep, giving the eye a firm place to land.
gen-gf-snowburst-one-gf-lexend-giga: Lexend Giga spaces its flat, single-weight letters so widely that each word opens up. But Snowburst One brings the stencil bridges above, and a long read below stays light, gentle and unhurried.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-lexend-peta: Outsized and a little wiry, Tektur opens every curve like a bent pipe cleaner. But Lexend Peta in sans does the quieter job, with wide-mouthed c shapes and a big x-height that settle into text.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-lexend-tera: Commanding from the first glance, Tilt Neon draws a tube-like stroke of constant width with a splayed c terminal and short ascenders. Lexend Tera, a plain sans, spaces its plotter-pen letters far apart.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-lexend-zetta: Unica One draws a very large lowercase eye, with daylight inside every curve and one stroke thickness throughout. And Lexend Zetta, in sans-serif, spreads out tall-bodied letters, so the heading earns its keep when big and short.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-montserrat-alternates: Montserrat Alternates reads with a wide-open c and round letters whose rims match the stems. Then Wallpoet lifts the line above in a sign-painter's-stencil flatness, a plain sans partner with high-rising lowercase.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-lexend-exa: Stretched, spacious and wholly without stroke contrast. Warnes tapers its ink strokes before they touch, while Lexend Exa, a sans with stubby ascenders and a big x-height, rewards a size a notch generous.
